derivedFrom: Shelly Gen2+ Virtual Components documentation for the Boolean component:

captured: Owner-captured filtered response, recorded below as capturedFilteredResponse:
GET /rpc/Shelly.GetComponents?keys=["switch:0","input:0","number:201","number:202"]
&include=["config","status"]
It establishes, on the installed device:
- the keys filter works, and returns switch:0, which was absent from the
first page of the unfiltered call;
- `total` under a keys filter is the number of MATCHED components (4 here),
not the device-wide count (20 unfiltered). Acceptance does not depend on
it either way; this is recorded so the semantics are no longer unknown;
- switch:0 carries status.output as a boolean, and input:0 status.state,
inside the components envelope;
- components are NOT returned in the requested order, so lookup must be by
key rather than by position;
- switch:0 config reports in_mode 'detached' and initial_state 'on'. The
owner changed initial_state to off on 2026-09-14 after this capture was
taken (Shelly UI: Action on power on -> Turn OFF). The capture below is
left exactly as recorded; it predates that change and still shows 'on'.
CORRECTION (2026-09-15): an earlier version of this note claimed the
detached in_mode satisfied a prerequisite shelly1/README.md names. It did
not name one - in_mode was undocumented until 2026-09-15, which is how it
came to regress unnoticed.
A fourth capture on 2026-09-15, same filtered request, recorded BOTH of these
back at their factory values on the same device: in_mode 'follow' and
initial_state 'restore_last', at cfg_rev 176 against 140 above. In follow the
firmware drives switch:0 from input:0 beneath the script, which is what made
the relay move while the bench page was only reading and flipping invert. The
lesson recorded here: these two switch:0 settings are not set-once, and any
test that assumes the script is the sole writer of RLY0 must confirm in_mode
first. That capture also showed input:0 healthy - type 'switch', enable true,
a boolean status.state - so the 'no boolean state' fault seen just before it
is not reproduced and remains unexplained.
The earlier unfiltered capture additionally showed @meta-declared components
carrying config.owner and attrs.role, and the unfiltered call paginating
(offset 0, total 20, twelve components returned).
Second and third owner-captured filtered responses, each naming five keys where
one does not exist on the device (number:203, then boolean:250):
the device SILENTLY OMITS the unknown key. No RPC error, no placeholder.
Four components returned and total 4 in both cases - total reports what the
filter matched, so an unknown key is indistinguishable from a truncated page
by the reply alone. Presence-checking every requested key is therefore the
only safe acceptance rule, and it is what the parser does.
Owner-captured acknowledgement, on this device over the same GET transport:
GET /rpc/Number.Set?id=201&value=0  ->  bare JSON null
Number.Set and Boolean.Set are sibling setters on the same virtual-component
RPC surface, so this corroborates the acknowledgement the dispatcher requires.
It is not literally Boolean.Set: that capture is still an acceptance check,
because no boolean component exists until the script is installed.
2026-09-15, the dynamic_only discovery call: Tab5IsLocked NOW EXISTS on the
device and is recorded below as capturedBooleanComponent. It matches the
documented Boolean shape this parser was written against - key 'boolean:<id>',
config.name exactly 'Tab5IsLocked', a boolean status.value, config.id carrying
the id - so the shape is no longer documentation-based. Its id is 200, which is
neither the 246 used in the fixtures below nor anything derivable, which is the
point: it is read from config.id and never assumed.
That capture also shows exactly three dynamic components, one per interface
name, with no duplicates - the condition normalize_shelly1_components requires.
2026-09-15, THE BOOLEAN.SET ACCEPTANCE CHECK, now captured on the device:
GET /rpc/Boolean.Set?id=200&value=true  ->  bare JSON null
Owner capture, browser address bar, Firefox JSON viewer rendering the body as
null. This is the literal shape _issue_boolean_set requires and the last of the
acknowledgement assumptions: the dispatcher accepts HTTP 200 with a body of
exactly null and rejects everything else as invalid-response. Captured against
a false-to-true transition, which is the only shape Tab5 ever issues - it
short-circuits on `if observed is value` and never writes a redundant value.
The HTTP status line was not in the captured frame, but a bare null is the
success reply on this RPC surface; an RPC error returns an error object.
2026-09-22, THE PROTECTION SCRIPT'S LIVENESS, captured on the bench in both
states and recorded below as capturedScriptComponentRunning and
capturedScriptComponentStopped. It establishes three things:
- script:1 comes back from the SAME filtered Shelly.GetComponents call the
cycle already makes, carrying both config and status. No second request.
That was the condition for reading liveness at all;
- status.running genuinely flips true -> false when the script is stopped,
unlike IsLocked and loCntr, which retain their last value and go on
looking healthy after their writer has stopped;
- config.enable stayed TRUE in the stopped capture. enable means 'should it
autostart', not 'is it executing', so running is the field read and enable
is never substituted for it.
The id is fixed in the request because scripts are NOT dynamic components: the
discovery call is dynamic_only=true and cannot resolve them by name. config.name
is therefore verified on every read, and a mismatch reads as absent. Script 2 on
this device is 'Test-Harness' with enable false; the owner may re-enable it, and
an id-only check would then be satisfied by the wrong script.
notCaptured: Observed relay behavior across a Shelly reboot with an inhibition outstanding.
Tab5IsLocked is persisted:false and anti-chatter.js seeds it false at startup,
so a Shelly reboot clears an outstanding inhibition and the relay closes when
the InitDelay window ends unless Tab5 has re-asserted by then. Whether Tab5's
reconciliation lands inside that window has never been observed. This is now
the ONLY outstanding item; every RPC shape this unit depends on is captured.
